articleHeadline: Circulating metabolites associated with protection against Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection and inhibition of mycobacterial growth - Communications Biology
articleSummary: Indonesia-based study of 199 heavily exposed TB household contacts who remained IGRA-negative. Researchers profiled circulating metabolites and metabolic genotypes to identify factors linked to protection from Mtb infection and to inhibition of mycobacterial growth. Differentially abundant metabolites pointed to pathways including arachidonic acid, arginine and proline, glutathione, and tryptophan metabolism, with negative IGRA at 3 months. SNPs near PRODH correlated with circulating proline levels and persistently negative IGRA; SNPs near AFMID associated with IGRA conversion. For validation, plasma metabolomics were linked to mycobacterial growth inhibition by peripheral blood mononuclear cells from individuals in a low-incidence setting. In this validation, lower concentrations of six metabolites, including leukotriene B4, proline, glycine, and tryptophan, aligned with stronger growth control and protection against IGRA conversion. Implication: circulating metabolites may shape innate defense against Mtb, suggesting metabolic interventions to prevent infection and disease.

articleSummary: Blitar's Kampung Coklat (Chocolate Village) in East Java, Indonesia, located at Jalan Banteng Blorok 18, Plosorejo, Kademangan, Blitar Regency, is a leading educational tourism site. The 6.5-hectare complex blends entertainment, education, culinary arts, and a cocoa plantation, featuring a chocolate gallery, dining area, rides, cooking classes, lodging, and a large visitor mosque. It operates its own chocolate processing plant with a capacity of up to three tons of finished chocolate daily, marketing to visitors and shipping to outside cities. articleSummary: South Africa pledges $2.5 million through the Africa Epidemics Fund to bolster Africa CDC's response to the Ebola outbreak driven by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of Congo (eastern provinces) and Uganda. The grant supports cross-border surveillance, decentralized isolation and treatment centers, cold-chain logistics for experimental therapeutics and potential vaccines, and real-time genomic sequencing, while providing hazard pay and psychosocial support to traumatized health staff. The Africa CDC frames the donation as a shift toward continental sovereignty in outbreak financing and responses to protect regional health security and trade corridors.

As of May 19, 536 suspected cases and 134 suspected deaths; over the past two days 26 confirmed and 143 suspected new cases. The outbreak is driven by the Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain, a rare type without vaccines or effective screening; only the Zaire vaccine may offer partial protection. Ebola viruses spread from wildlife (likely fruit bats) to humans, then via blood, saliva and body fluids between people. Typical symptoms include fever, extreme fatigue, muscle pains, headaches, vomiting, diarrhea, rash, and bleeding; case fatality can reach about 50%. Four strains infect humans: Zaire, Sudan, Bundibugyo, Tai Forest. Diagnostics may miss Bundibugyo; no approved treatment. DRC has deployed teams to Bunia; WHO and MSF are on scene. WHO funds $3.9 million; the U.S. pledges 2,300 USD (about NT$7.26 billion) to aid Congo and Uganda.

articleSummary: Two concurrent outbreaks in weeks highlight global health response gaps: Andes hantavirus linked to a cruise ship MV Hondius in the southern Atlantic (hantavirus is endemic to Argentina, with Ushuaia departures), and the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ituri region near Uganda and South Sudan. The outbreak began in early April 2026, as reported by a local farmer, Ketut Widanta, whose pigs—each about 150 kg and ready for market—refused food, became lethargic, collapsed, and died. The animals were buried, and the farmer has ceased pig rearing temporarily while planning pen cleaning to remove potential contaminants. Badung’s Agriculture and Food Service Office has not publicly confirmed the incident or taken action. The report notes the virus is suspected to be ASF and that the disease had previously disappeared before reappearing, signaling an ongoing, localized outbreak in the Bali region as of 21 May 2026.

articleHeadline: 姐弟俩被狗咬，姐姐隐瞒患狂犬病去世，什么时候需要打狂犬疫苗？
articleSummary: Rabies is nearly 100% fatal after symptom onset. In Hunan, China, an 11-year-old girl and her younger brother were bitten by a domestic white mongrel dog that suddenly became aggressive in December. The younger brother sought wound cleansing, vaccination, and rabies immunoglobulin at a township clinic; the sister concealed the bite, did not wash the wound, and did not receive vaccine. In February, she developed hydrophobia and aerophobia, followed by throat spasms and paralysis, was hospitalized with suspected rabies, and died within 48 hours of symptom onset. Saliva testing confirmed rabies virus infection. Globally, about 99% of human rabies cases result from dog bites; other animals include cats, bats, foxes, wolves, and raccoons. Incubation is typically 1–3 months. Post-exposure vaccination is guided by exposure level; Level II requires wound care and vaccination, Level III includes passive immunization. Start vaccination early; full regimen is preferred, and use the same-brand vaccine if possible.

articleSummary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri Province, Ebola has killed more than 130 people in what is the 17th outbreak there, but caused by the Bundibugyo virus variant—only the third time laboratory-confirmed for this strain. There is no licensed vaccine or targeted therapy for Bundibugyo; the WHO is evaluating whether existing Ebola medicines might work against this variant. The outbreak appears to have started several months earlier and remained under the radar, with early symptoms resembling flu or malaria, delaying diagnosis; standard Ebola tests do not reliably detect Bundibugyo. The epicenter lies in Ituri near the Uganda and South Sudan borders, a conflict-affected and hard-to-reach area. Traditional funeral rites—washing and kissing the deceased—facilitate transmission. The WHO has raised the second-highest alert level, but experts do not expect a pandemic, since transmission requires direct contact with bodily fluids.

articleSummary: Ebola re-emerges with the Bundibugyo strain driving current infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda. Bundibugyo mortality is estimated at 25–50%, lower than the deadliest Zaïre and Sudan strains (up to ~90%). Incubation is short—typically a few days to two weeks—and symptoms rapidly progress from high fever and severe weakness to vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain and bleeding. Transmission is not airborne; it occurs mainly via direct contact with infected bodily fluids. Local funeral practices can fuel spread, prompting WHO to call for safe and dignified burials. Despite dramatic images, experts say the global pandemic risk is low; over 50 years there have been about 40 major outbreaks, with European or U.S. importations being rare. WHO designated the outbreak a Public Health Emergency of International Concern, with highest risk in the DRC and Uganda. Poland advised against travel to border areas with DR Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan. No effective vaccine against Bundibugyo exists.

Berlin’s decision cited shorter flight time and specialized treatment options.

If uninfected, vaccination is advised because HBV vaccination is one of the few vaccines that helps prevent cancer. The standard childhood schedule is three doses at birth, 2 months, and 6 months, with an additional dose at 1 month and hepatitis B immunoglobulin after birth if the mother is an HBV carrier. The vaccine program has provided free HBV vaccination for newborns since 1992, alongside other vaccines.

articleSummary: Ebola fears prompted a diversion of Air France Flight 378 after departure from Paris; the US authorities blocked the plane from landing at Detroit Metropolitan Airport, with Air France confirming the flight was redirected to Montreal Trudeau International at the request of US authorities around 5:00 pm ET. No urgent medical cases were reported aboard. Concurrently, the CDC announced entry restrictions for travelers who recently visited Congo, South Sudan, or Uganda within the past 21 days, effective for 30 days. All US-bound flights carrying such passengers will be redirected to Washington Dulles International Airport in Virginia for processing. The measures, described as precautionary against Ebola risk, take effect today and apply to individuals arriving from these three countries within the 21-day window. No laboratory confirmations are cited in the report.

articleHeadline: ایبولا وائرس نے پوری دنیا کیلئے خطرے کی گھنٹی بجا دی پاکستان میں بھی ہائی الرٹ جاری
articleSummary: As of May 21, 2026, Ebola virus disease has triggered global alarm with the World Health Organization designating the outbreak a global public health concern. Pakistan's Ministry of Health has initiated pre-emptive measures, instructing the National Institute of Health to implement necessary actions and keep laboratory kits in stock. Border Health Services are to stay alert, with enhanced airport surveillance for passengers arriving from Uganda and Congo. Ebola symptoms can resemble hemorrhagic fever and may be mistaken for dengue, so clinicians are advised to remain cautious. Pakistani officials say the situation is fully under control and no widespread concern is warranted. In Africa, approximately 300 suspected Ebola cases and 80 deaths have been reported in the two affected countries, with a U.S. CDC team deployed to assist.

articleHeadline: Ebola Alert Issued at RGIA for Flyers Arriving from High-Risk Countries
articleSummary: As of 21 May 2026, an Ebola alert is issued at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) in Shamshabad, Hyderabad, with a health advisory for passengers arriving from high-risk countries—Democratic Republic of Congo, Uganda, and South Sudan. The advisory by APHO and DGHS directs travellers with symptoms or exposure history to report to airport health authorities before immigration clearance. Symptoms to watch include fever, weakness, headache, muscle pain, vomiting, diarrhoea, sore throat and unexplained bleeding; those who had direct contact with blood or body fluids of suspected or confirmed Ebola patients should report immediately. Any traveller developing symptoms within 21 days of arrival should seek immediate care and disclose travel history. Delhi airport has displayed the advisory. A high-level meeting chaired by Union Health Secretary Punya Salila Srivastava reviewed preparedness; no Ebola cases have been detected in India. India has strengthened surveillance and SOPs for pre/post-arrival screening, quarantine, case management, and lab testing across states and UTs.

articleHeadlineTranslated: An Ebola outbreak forces the Democratic Republic of the Congo national team to move its training camp abroad.
articleHeadline: تفشي فيروس إيبولا يدفع منتخب الكونغو الديمقراطية لنقل معسكره خارج البلاد
articleSummary: The Democratic Republic of Congo's national football team canceled its three-day training camp in Kinshasa due to an Ebola outbreak in eastern DRC, with the camp subsequently moved to Belgium. Health authorities reported the outbreak is the 17th Ebola surge in the country’s history, with about 600 suspected cases and 139 deaths. It remains unclear whether Ebola drove the camp relocation, according to a team spokesperson. The United States confirmed that Congo will be allowed to participate in the 2026 FIFA World Cup in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, scheduled from June 11 to July 19, 2026. Congo's World Cup group is Group 11, alongside Portugal, Uzbekistan, and Colombia. The article notes the current squad listing includes players from abroad and does not feature players from the domestic league.

articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: The international response to Ebola is taking shape in Ituri.
articleHeadline: Congo-Kinshasa: La réponse internationale contre Ebola s'organise en Ituri
articleSummary: Ebola virus disease is actively spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ituri province, with about 140 deaths and around 600 suspected cases under surveillance across four health zones—Bunia, Rwampara, Mungwalu, and Nyakunde. The World Health Organization regards the epidemic’s regional risk as high for Central Africa but low globally, noting the outbreak likely began several months ago. UNICEF delivered 16 tonnes of preventive medical kits by air to Bunia on May 19, the second shipment after May 17, to enable rapid response and patient care. Authorities pledge sustained support until the outbreak is defeated, urging communities to maintain hygiene and avoid unsafe funeral practices. Security remains precarious: an ADF attack in Alima, Mambasa territory, killed 17 civilians, highlighting challenging conditions for response efforts.
notes: 記事サマリーはDRCのイトゥリ州でのエボラ流行を主題としており、ルワンダのキガリ州も発生地域に含まれているが、サマリー上ではDRCのみが確認される。WHOは地域的リスクは高いが世界的リスクは低いと評価している。セキュリティ上の課題（武装勢力の攻撃）が対応を複雑化させている。

articleHeadline: Россия поможет взять под контроль вспышку Эболы в Африке после смерти 139 человек
articleSummary: As of May 21, 2026, Russian scientists and authorities will assist residents of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda in containing the Ebola outbreak, following 139 deaths reported from the epidemic. The aid was announced by Maria Zakharova, spokesperson for the Russian Foreign Ministry, at a briefing, framing the effort as urgent and time-sensitive. The report characterizes the Ebola outbreak as ongoing in Africa, with Russia pledging rapid support to help bring the situation under control in DRC and Uganda. The article centers on the death toll and international assistance; no further clinical or transmission details are provided.

articleHeadline: Africa Takes Action After Ebola Outbreak
articleSummary: As of 2026-05-21, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has claimed over 134 lives and Spread to Uganda, prompting Africa-wide action to curb cross-border transmission. South Africa pledged $2.5 million through the Africa CDC Africa Epidemics Fund to bolster regional health security. Rwanda dispatched response teams to border crossings, established isolation centres to monitor returning residents, and stepped up contact tracing. Kenya has screened more than 34,500 travelers at airports, seaports and land borders, while ruling out blanket quarantines. Nigeria’s Federal Airports Authority is collaborating with the country’s disease control agency to isolate and assess any suspected cases at points of entry. The article emphasizes coordinated border-focused measures to contain Ebola spread, highlighting surveillance, isolation, and risk mitigation at entry points to prevent further transmission across Africa.
